artifacts.title: FTP write to ASPX webshell and JuicyPotato SYSTEM (Devel)
artifacts.starting_access: unauthenticated access to FTP and IIS on a Windows 7 / Server 2008 R2
artifacts.outcome: NT AUTHORITY/SYSTEM via SeImpersonatePrivilege and JuicyPotato
transferable_properties: FTP anonymous + IIS with web-root mapping gives instant webshell when write is allowed
check shell architecture before downloading tools, IIS app pools often run x86
IIS 7.5 maps to Windows 7/2008 R2 which maps to JuicyPotato
SeImpersonatePrivilege on IIS shells is by design
certutil is the most reliable download method on old Windows

observations: FTP root maps to the IIS web root

hypotheses.statement: FTP write access to the web root lets us upload an executable ASPX file

selected_action.intent: confirm FTP write access and enumerate the web root

evidence.summary: confirmed FTP anonymous write access by uploading test.txt visible over HTTP

hypotheses.statement: uploading an ASPX reverse shell and triggering it over HTTP yields a shell

selected_action.intent: generate an ASPX reverse shell, upload via FTP, and trigger via HTTP

evidence.summary: uploaded shell.aspx and triggered it over HTTP for a shell as iis apppool/web

hypotheses.statement: a x86 JuicyPotato abuses DCOM/BITS to impersonate SYSTEM

selected_action.intent: download the x86 JuicyPotato and nc.exe and run the token impersonation exploit

evidence.summary: ran x86 JuicyPotato with the BITS CLSID and obtained NT AUTHORITY/SYSTEM

execution_examples.capability_hint: privilege escalation via SeImpersonatePrivilege and JuicyPotato token impersonation
execution_examples.purpose: escalate from an IIS app pool to NT AUTHORITY/SYSTEM via DCOM/BITS token impersonation

prerequisites.statement: the shell has SeImpersonatePrivilege and the JuicyPotato architecture matches
